key_insight: Cavitated front gridline Ag paste reduces series-resistance-related fill-factor loss in PERC solar cells, but performance is limited by nonuniform current access at the metal/contact interface.
engineering_relevance: The study points to metallization/interfacial quality as a key lever for improving PERC cell efficiency by lowering extraction losses without changing Voc or Jsc.
method: Fabricated 15 large-area (252 cm2) PERC cells with cavitated silver paste.
Compared electrical metrics with electroluminescence, SEM/STEM, and conductive AFM.
Examined cross-sections and sequential layer removal to probe contact heterogeneity.
evidence_signal: Across the 15 cells, mean efficiency was 21.87% with a best of 22.07%, and fill factor dropped as area-normalized series resistance increased from 0.53 to 0.83 ohm-cm2 while Voc and Jsc stayed nearly unchanged.
watch_item: The benefits depend on maintaining uniform conductive pathways; localized interfacial defects or inconsistent glass/Ag connectivity can still create voltage drops and limit fill-factor gains.
paper_title: Progress in Cavitated Front Gridline Ag Paste for PERC Solar Cell Architecture
